newsitem.title: USA: US ag attache-India 97/8 cotton crop, exports down.
newsitem.headline: US ag attache-India 97/8 cotton crop, exports down.

text.p: An agricultural attache at the American embassy in New Delhi forecast India 1997/98 cotton production would dip to 12.1 million 480-pound bales from 12.8 million bales in 1996/97.

In a report dated June 20 released in Washington on Monday, the attache also forecast cotton exports would drop dramatically as tight ending stocks, strong domestic consumption, and higher prices limited the size of the export quota and export volumes.
The attache pegged India 1997/98 cotton exports at 234,000 bales, down sharply from about one million bales in 1996/97.

On production, the attache said weak 1996/97 prices were likely to result in lower area. Yields were also expected to fall slightly based on the assumption that winter weather will be normal in central India, the attache wrote in the report.
Attache reports are not official USDA data. USDA has not issued a forecast for the India 1997/98 cotton crop.
